surfaces.label: Clay - smooth / groomed
surfaces.note: Watered and groomed indoor clay; very high, consistent grip that blue-grooves along the racing line.

surfaces.label: Clay - dry / dusty
surfaces.note: Clay that has dried out; a dust film cuts side-bite and makes grip line-dependent.

surfaces.label: Hard-packed dirt
surfaces.note: Compacted abrasive dirt; high grip but eats pins, favors long-wear compounds and low-profile treads.

surfaces.label: Blue groove (rubbered hard pack)
surfaces.note: Rubber laid into hard pack forms a dark groove; huge grip on line, slick off line.

surfaces.label: Dusty blue groove
surfaces.note: Blue groove with loose dust on top; grip improves as the line cleans, very inconsistent early in the day.

surfaces.label: Loose dirt / loam
surfaces.note: Fresh, moist loamy soil; moderate diggy grip, full-pin tires bite well, surface evolves fast.

surfaces.label: Sugar / fluffy dirt
surfaces.note: Dry powdery 'sugar' surface; very low grip, polishes tires, soft compounds and big pins needed.

surfaces.label: Grass
surfaces.note: Slippery with high rolling resistance; full spikes work best, grip drops sharply when wet.

surfaces.label: Astroturf (artificial turf)
surfaces.note: UK/EU-style astro; consistent medium-high grip, abrasive on pins, low-profile mini-pin territory.

surfaces.label: Carpet offroad (EOS style)
surfaces.note: Indoor needle-pile race carpet; extreme consistent grip, traction-rolling risk, hard mini-pin or slick tires.

surfaces.label: Mixed astro + dirt
surfaces.note: UK-style mixed sections of turf and dirt; compromise tire and setup between both surfaces.

surfaces.label: Wood / plywood sections
surfaces.note: Wood ramps and flooring sections on indoor tracks; low slippery grip, sensitive to dust.

surfaces.label: Sand
surfaces.note: Very low grip, car digs in; paddle or full-spike tires, grip improves slightly when damp.

surfaces.label: Gravel
surfaces.note: Loose stones over base; low unpredictable grip (rally-style), harsh on tires and drivetrain.

surfaces.label: Mud / wet dirt
surfaces.note: Wet sticky soil that clogs treads; open full-pin or cut-stagger treads to self-clean.

surfaces.label: Snow
surfaces.note: Very low grip and cold tires; spikes or paddles, compounds stay too hard in cold.

surfaces.label: Ice
surfaces.note: Minimal grip; studded or pin tires required, throttle and steering inputs must be tiny.

surfaces.label: Asphalt - low grip (green/dusty)
surfaces.note: Unrubbered or dusty asphalt (parking lot); low traction, softer compounds and additive needed.

surfaces.label: Asphalt - high grip (rubbered/treated)
surfaces.note: Rubbered-in or sugar/traction-treated race asphalt; very high grip, harder compounds, traction-roll watch.

surfaces.label: Tarmac street circuit
surfaces.note: Public-road tarmac; variable bumpy grip with dust and crowning, durability matters.

surfaces.label: Carpet onroad (ETS/CRC)
surfaces.note: ETS-style black carpet or CRC ozite; extreme consistent grip, dedicated carpet compounds (e.g. 28 shore) and stiff sidewalls.

surfaces.label: Painted / sealed concrete
surfaces.note: Paint-sealed concrete; medium grip that builds with rubber, slippery when cold or dusty.

surfaces.label: Polished concrete
surfaces.note: Smooth polished slab; low-to-medium grip, very sensitive to dust and tire additive.

surfaces.label: Rough concrete (unpainted)
surfaces.note: Bare rough concrete; medium grip but very abrasive, accelerated tire wear.

surfaces.label: RCP foam tile (mini scale)
surfaces.note: Interlocking foam tile (Mini-Z/RCP); moderate predictable grip for small scales, wears in over time.

spring_systems.identification: Paint color on coil + length class (S/M/L); rate rises through the color chart; XGS part numbers for 1/8, IF/XGS for MP9/MP10
examples: 1/8 S-length: Gold = Medium (XGS003), Red = Medium Hard (XGS004), Yellow = Hard (XGS005), Orange = Super Hard (XGS006)
1/10 big bore: Green 9T 3.1 lb/in -> Grey 8T 3.6 -> Blue 7.5T 3.9 -> Yellow 7T 4.3 -> Red 6.5T 4.6 -> Orange 6T 5.1 lb/in

spring_systems.identification: Touring: 'C=' spring constant printed on package (4S springs, 20mm, hand-matched pairs); 1/8 offroad: number of paint dots (1-5) identifies rate, sets offered linear and progressive
examples: T4/X4 4S linear sets: C=2.1, C=2.3, C=2.6, C=3.0
4S progressive sets: C=2.3-2.6, C=2.5-2.8 (rate rises through stroke)
XB8 front 69mm progressive springs: 3-dot, 4-dot, 5-dot; rear 82mm: 2-dot etc.

spring_systems.identification: Paint color per spring family with rate in lb/in on AE's published spring rate charts (12mm, 13mm V2, 1/8 RC8 big bore)
examples: 13mm V2 buggy springs: color-coded (grey/blue/yellow/green/red/orange/white) spanning roughly 3-6 lb/in
RC8 1/8 springs listed by rate + color on AE 1/8 off-road spring list
Same color can mean different rates across families - always check the chart by spring series

spring_systems.identification: Rate in lb/in with color paint stripe; separate standard and Low Frequency (LF) spring lines (LF = softer initial feel for high-grip tracks)
examples: TLR 22-series 12mm springs by lb/in + color stripe
LF spring sets for carpet/astro high-bite conditions

spring_systems.identification: Linear springs = constant coil pitch, one rate through the stroke; progressive springs = variable pitch, rate increases with compression (soft initial, firm bottoming); identify by uneven coil spacing or dual-rate markings
examples: Progressive: predictable on bumpy outdoor tracks, resists bottoming
Linear: consistent feel preferred on smooth high-grip indoor tracks
Stiffer springs front = more on-power steering exit; stiffer rear = more steering into corner, less forward traction
